svg.title: Senolytics (D+Q, fisetin): what has actually been tested
svg.desc: Senolytics (D+Q, fisetin): what has actually been tested. Regulatory status (US): Dasatinib: prescription leukemia drug. Quercetin, fisetin: supplements. None approved for aging. Verdict: Not approved for aging. Lifespan in old mice: D+Q raised post-treatment survival (2018); fisetin extended median and maximum lifespan (2018). Verdict: Strong animal signal. Lifespan in people: No human trial has tested whether senolytics extend life. Verdict: Not tested. Clearing senescent cells in people: Fewer senescent cells in fat and skin in a 9-person open-label pilot (2019). Verdict: Early, uncontrolled. Lung, brain and bone trials (D+Q): Lung and Alzheimer's pilots: feasible, no clear benefit; bone trial missed its main goal. Verdict: Mostly negative. Fibrotic fatty liver (D+Q): 31-person placebo-controlled phase 2 met its main goal on biopsy (Oct 2026). Verdict: One positive trial. Fisetin in people: 75-person knee-arthritis trial: no difference vs placebo; Mayo AFFIRM trials unreported. Verdict: No benefit shown yet. Safety: More side effects on D+Q in placebo-controlled trials; dasatinib carries serious label warnings. Verdict: Real drug risks.
